adapter.nonSuccessOutcome: An empty, non-numeric, zero-length (for Length) or unchanged value is silently ignored, matching the existing guards in updateLength/updateAngle/updateFeedFenceOffsetValue (LineForm.functions.ts:37-100); no error state is rendered.
forbiddenAccess: DOM queries outside the mounted host node
Stores.lines / Stores.shapes global state beyond the values passed in as adapter inputs
ElementCreationManager and FloorPlanMaker.history APIs directly; these stay behind the adapter commands that LineForm.tsx already implements

lifecycle: The Angular application is created with createApplication() and mounted with createComponent() from a React effect on a ref, per docs\project-constants.md#Embedding
The same React effect destroys the Angular application on unmount
The host effect re-supplies all adapter inputs and forces a resync whenever the selected line's id changes, since RichLine identity is not itself an Angular input
Change detection is zoneless via provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection(), per docs\project-constants.md#Change-detection
styling: Templates are inline in @Component, never a separate .html file, per docs\project-constants.md#Compilation

scenarios.given: A line is selected and the Length field shows its current real length (LineForm.tsx:128-145).
scenarios.when: The map editor enters a new, valid, changed length value.
then: The line's real length updates via RichLine.updateLength.
Distance lines are cleared and recreated for the single line.
A history entry is added only when the change was key-driven.

scenarios.given: A line is selected and the Angle field shows its current angle (LineForm.tsx:147-158).
scenarios.when: The map editor enters a new, valid angle value.
then: The line's real angle updates via RichLine.updateAngle.
Distance lines are cleared and recreated for the single line.

scenarios.given: The active robot has the FeedPush capability, so the Fence offset selector renders (LineForm.tsx:160-185).
scenarios.when: The map editor chooses None, Left or Right.
then: line.fenceOffset updates to the chosen value.
A history entry is always added, unlike the key-gated Length and Angle edits.

scenarios.given: Fence offset is Left or Right, so the fence-offset distance field renders (LineForm.tsx:186-205).
scenarios.when: The map editor enters a new, valid offset distance.

scenarios.given: The active robot lacks the FeedPush capability.
scenarios.when: The Detail Drawer renders the selected or in-progress line.
then: The Fence offset label, selector and distance field do not render at all.

scenarios.given: The map editor has finished adjusting Length, Angle and/or Fence offset for a single, non-creation line selection.
scenarios.when: The map editor clicks the retained Done button.
then: onDone() enforces a minimum length default, deselects elements, refreshes the lines store and writes a Move history item.
The drawer closes because MapMakerManager.deselectElements() clears the selection.

scenarios.given: The user pressed a key that cleared the Length field to empty or zero after a nonzero valid length.
then: The last valid length is restored through two infinitesimal nudges so the bound input value prop changes and re-renders.

characterizationRequired.hypothesis: The migrated fields must reproduce FocusNumberInput's 300ms onChange debounce and its suspension of global keyboard shortcuts (Delete/Backspace) while focused, or typing in a migrated field will behave differently from every other detail-drawer field.

The displayed Length, and the offset distance, are real.length/fenceOffsetValue doubled (map-unit-to-cm conversion tied to the line being represented symmetrically); the Angular adapter must apply and reverse this doubling exactly, not just pass values through.

Length and Angle only push an undo/redo history entry when isInputKeyPressed is true, so a programmatic restore (restoreLengthIfInvalid) must not itself create unwanted history entries; the Angular command boundary must preserve this distinction rather than always recording history like the Fence offset commands do.

While the line being edited is still the one actively being drawn (ElementCreationManager.lineCreator.line?.id() === line.id()), editing Length or Angle must call secondClickHandler() instead of the normal refresh/history path; the Angular command boundary must preserve this branch rather than always taking the normal-edit path.

decisions.topic: Slice boundary for the Detail Drawer LineForm flow
decisions.decision: Angular owns Length, Angle and the Fence offset selector plus its distance field; LineForm.tsx (as mounting host), the Selected Line label, LineRiskCard, the Detectable section, Coordinates/Distances, DoneButton and NavbarDeleteMapElement stay in React.
decisions.rationale: Of the three candidates evaluated, this is the only one that satisfies all four boundary criteria (one owner, no shared infrastructure in the write allowlist, a measurable retained neighbour, bounded branches) while covering the literal user-visible goal. Length+Angle-only under-covers the stated Fence offset requirement. A full LineForm replacement would pull DoneButton and NavbarDeleteMapElement into the cut, both generic detail-drawer chrome shared by every other object type (11 external importers each), and would leave no retain-react sibling to compare visual parity against.
decisions.followUp: A later slice may migrate the Detectable section or the Coordinates section, each of which already has a retained sibling of its own kind (RadioButtonWithIcon family, FocusNumberInput family) to compare against.

decisions.topic: Reuse of shared React input and radio components
decisions.decision: FocusNumberInput.tsx (12 external importers) and RadioButtonGroup/RadioButton/RadioButtonWithIcon (26 external importers) stay untouched; the Angular fields reproduce their appearance and debounce/keyboard-shortcut-suspension behavior independently instead of editing or wrapping them.
decisions.rationale: Editing either shared file would change behavior for every other detail-drawer form (chargerForm, cornerStripForm, dumpStationForm, lidarForm, and others), which is outside this flow's ownership.

testGaps: LineForm.tsx's own render and branching logic (the hasCapability gates, tab order, and the set-first-point placeholder branch) has no automated test; only the pure functions in LineForm.functions.ts are covered by __tests__/LineForm.functions.test.ts.
No automated test proves the 300ms debounce or the Escape/keyboard-shortcut-suspension timing that FocusNumberInput.tsx documents in its own comments.

Per-flow coverage for lineForm/__tests__/LineForm.functions.test.ts was not retrieved this run; CI computes it via npm run test:ci and uploads coverage/lcov.info to the Lely-Route-Assistant-Frontend SonarQube project.

manualValidation.environment: Route Assistant desktop application running the local frontend and local backend, title bar showing 'localhost' and 'react mode: development' badges, per docs\project-constants.md#Manual-verification-environment.
manualValidation.scenario: Select an existing line, then separately draw a new one with one point placed: edit Length to a new value and confirm the map line resizes; edit Angle and confirm the map line rotates; on a robot with FeedPush capability, switch Fence offset between None/Left/Right, edit its distance value, and confirm the offset line updates and that the Fence offset controls are absent on a robot without that capability; clear the Length field and blur it to confirm the last valid value is restored; click Done and confirm the drawer closes with the edits applied and undo/redo still working.

rollback: Revert only the files listed in scope.allowedWritePaths (LineForm.tsx, the new lineForm/angular directory, any additions under lineForm/__tests__, package.json, package-lock.json and tsconfig.json) to their state at revision ab76866c89d2709fd5ed4b079b22dff80c419883. Do not revert any other detail-drawer form, FocusNumberInput.tsx, or the RadioButton family, since this slice never touches them. After reverting, run npm install once to drop the @angular/* packages from node_modules.
